sixBar.independentContract: The b1c975af historical failure and updated retrieval design §4.2 query-by-example semantics require unlike to steer order while keeping matches above the positive target minimum and excluding input IDs. It must not empty valid narrow-cone matches by moving the target.
sixBar.realRegression: Restoring target = normalize(mean(like) − 0.5*mean(unlike)) moves the target outside the supplied high-common-component fixture cone. Both independently known matching candidates then disappear below the configured 0.9 minimum; expected [a,b] fails against an empty result.
sixBar.independentOracle: Four authored unit-vector inputs use fixed literals; both candidates have known positive cosine 0.91 above the explicitly supplied 0.9 floor. The expected IDs are literal [ke_candidateaa1,ke_candidatebb1], independent of any earlier search response, production dot/mean/ranking helper or FakeEmbedder word hashing. Result order is sorted because membership is this case’s unique contract.
sixBar.stableSeam: KnowledgeSearch.start/idle/search/stop with the real disk-backed index, vector/candidate/ranking implementation and a KnowledgeEmbedder port supplying fixed external model answers. Only the external neural inference dependency is replaced; the fake does not return a ranked result.
sixBar.refactorResistance: No private exampleSearch call, target-vector shape, production score formula or helper export is observed. Any implementation that preserves the positive model floor and returned candidate membership passes.
sixBar.uniqueProtection: The existing two-dimensional query-by-example owner protects directional steering, input exclusion, combined query signals and validation at a 0.1 floor; it does not expose the historical high-floor/narrow-cone collapse. The expensive opt-in real-model gate cannot replace this always-running exact membership witness.

sixBar.independentContract: Retrieval design P0.4 retains recall@5 ≥0.8 and calibrated model thresholds. The updated query-by-example contract and b1c975af real-model bug report require a rejected hooks example to move its independently authored near-copy down without making that known matching repost unavailable.
sixBar.realRegression: The deployed sentence model’s actual geometry, pooling or threshold integration can make unlike searches empty, discard a known valid repost or fail to demote the negative example’s near-copy even when simple fixed-vector steering passes. Existing bilingual recall and duplicate/related-topic calibration failures remain visible.
sixBar.independentOracle: Existing human-authored expected query answers and literal quality bounds remain. The corpus explicitly labels ke_tiktok_hooks_repost as a near-copy of ke_tiktok_hooks; the named repost must exist in both returned lists and move downward under that negative example. Only the independently specified direction is compared, never a copied scoring formula or exact incidental rank. Both index lookups are guarded against -1. No whole expected result set is calculated from a prior search output. Input-ID exclusion remains at the existing cheaper deterministic owner instead of being duplicated in this actual-model block.
sixBar.stableSeam: Actual OnnxSentenceEmbedder and the pinned model files through the existing eval harness and real KnowledgeSearch public requests. The new EvalSearch.entries method forwards the typed public request and returns actual entry IDs; it does not simulate rank behavior.
sixBar.refactorResistance: No exact 5th/22nd position, native tensor shape, private vector state, score formula or factory identity is asserted. Model/index internals may change while satisfying independently authored relevance/quality and qualitative steering requirements.
sixBar.uniqueProtection: The cheap geometric cases isolate algorithmic membership and steering; they cannot establish that the shipped pinned model’s narrow similarity distribution still works with actual pooling, thresholds and the hand-judged corpus. Existing recall-only queries do not exercise unlike. Reusing this already-loaded model/index avoids a second expensive opt-in startup.
